audit.whatIsWrong: Illaoi's W and E are swapped everywhere they are labelled. spikes[0].text writes "Test of Spirit (W)" and "Harsh Lesson (E)"; spikes[1].text refers to "her E-pull"; mid says "her E reset".
audit.why: Data Dragon has Harsh Lesson on W (the 4s leap-and-strike attack reset) and Test of Spirit on E (the 900-range spirit rip). Every slot letter in this matchup is on the wrong ability, and the suspectNames pass could not catch it because the NAMES are spelled correctly — only the letters are wrong. A player reading "her E reset" watches the wrong ability come off cooldown.
audit.corrected: Harsh Lesson is W (4s, attack reset). Test of Spirit is E (16s at rank 1, 900 range).

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit is described as a pull — "her E-pull" in spikes[1].text, and "Her vessel pull. Sidestep it." in dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Illaoi rips the spirit from a foe's body, forcing it to stand before her." Nothing displaces Zac. What actually happens is that the spirit echoes a percentage of the damage it takes back to him, and if the spirit is killed or he walks too far from it he becomes a Vessel that spawns tentacles. Calling it a pull hides the real decision — what to do about the spirit once it is out.
audit.corrected: It rips a spirit, it does not displace you; the spirit echoes damage to you, and it dying or you leaving it turns you into a Vessel.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says Leap of Faith "spawns a ring of tentacles that shred you" and calls it "a death sentence".
audit.why: Riot's text: "A Tentacle spawns for each enemy champion hit." In a solo lane that is one champion and therefore one tentacle. Her ultimate is a teamfight multiplier, not a 1v1 execute — the thing that actually kills Zac in this lane is the tentacle field she already has up. Overstating the ult teaches a Zac player to give up a lane he can still play.
audit.corrected: One tentacle per champion hit — solo, that is one. The existing field is the threat, not the ult.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing explains WHY tentacles swing at Zac during a normal trade.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God: "Tentacles swing at spirits, Vessels, and victims of Illaoi's Harsh lesson." Harsh Lesson (W) is the trigger, and it is on a flat 4s cooldown — so the tentacle damage is not ambient, it is gated behind a 4-second ability. That is the cooldown a Zac player should actually be counting.
audit.corrected: Harsh Lesson (W), 4s flat, is what makes nearby tentacles swing at you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json (Prophet of an Elder God, Harsh Lesson)

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is never mentioned in the content layer.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God: tentacles "will heal Illaoi if they damage a champion". Against a tank who intends to stay in melee that healing is the whole reason extended trades are lost, and _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds — her tentacles heal her every time they damage a champion.

notes:
DO NOT USE two _missing-interactions.json headlines for this matchup — both rest on a bad derived flag. (1) "Illaoi can deny your mobility (Elastic Slingshot (E)) with Leap of Faith (R)": Illaoi's R is flagged "grounding" only because build-kit-library.js matches /grounds?\b/ against Riot's phrase "smashes her idol into the ground". (2) "Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Illaoi's Harsh Lesson (W)": Zac's E is flagged grounding for the same reason — "attaches his arms to the ground". Neither ability grounds anything. I wrote no text depending on either, and recommend the grounding rule in tools/build-kit-library.js be tightened to require a verb form ("grounds", "grounded") rather than the noun.

The autoreset flag on Harsh Lesson (W) IS genuine and I used it.

WKM_LINES to verify (champion-level, illaoi line 1): "If she rips your soul (E), leave the lane radius." Riot says the target becomes a Vessel if it "gets too far from the spirit", so walking away may be what triggers the Vessel rather than escaping it. The slot letter (E) is correct, which is worth noting given the zac matchup text had it as W.
